claim: Auto-regressive LLMs cannot, by themselves, do planning or self-verification.
The paper concludes that LLMs are useful only as front-end/back-end format translators that hand problems off to external symbolic solvers.
note: TRAP: that view is named in the abstract but explicitly called over-pessimistic/misguided.

claim: Without external feedback, LLMs struggle to self-correct their reasoning and at times perform even worse after self-correction.
The paper demonstrates that fine-tuning on self-correction data restores an LLM's ability to self-correct its reasoning.
note: TRAP: plausible remedy never stated in the abstract.

claim: In their reasoning and planning experiments they observed significant performance collapse with self-critique and significant gains with a sound external verifier.
Their experiments found that LLM self-critique improves performance more than using an external verifier.
note: TRAP: direct inversion of the finding.

claim: SciFact is a dataset of about 1.4K expert-written scientific claims paired with evidence-containing abstracts annotated with labels and rationales.
SciFact contains over 100,000 expert-written scientific claims.
The SciFact baseline models achieve over 90% F1 on scientific claim verification.
note: TRAP: plausible metric the abstract never states.

claim: The paper finds a linear correlation between an LLM's self-recognition capability and the strength of its self-preference bias.
The authors conclude that self-preference bias is unrelated to whether an LLM can recognize its own outputs.
note: TRAP: contradicts the causal link the paper reports.

claim: Restricting an LLM to structured formats such as JSON significantly declines its reasoning ability, and stricter constraints cause greater degradation.
JSONSchemaBench shows that XGrammar is the fastest of the constrained-decoding frameworks it evaluates.
note: TRAP: XGrammar is among the six evaluated, but the abstract states no speed ranking.

claim: JSONSchemaBench comprises about 10K real-world JSON schemas and evaluates six state-of-the-art constrained-decoding frameworks.
Cognitive forcing interventions significantly reduced overreliance compared to simple explainable-AI approaches, but received the least favorable subjective ratings.
Adding explanations to the AI's decisions reliably reduces people's overreliance on the AI.
note: TRAP: the abstract says explanations do NOT reduce overreliance and may increase it.
